headline: High: Plandex can write/modify shared project state while the paired sample repo offers no isolation or safeguards, creating conflict and injection risk if outputs are bridged.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Plandex reads and writes a project directory and uses a review-then-apply workflow with optional auto-apply; if spring-integration-samples content is copied into that workspace, untrusted text can be treated as instructions. The pair has no documented shared channel, so this is inferred rather than directly observed.
conditions: IF spring-integration-samples content is placed into Plandex's project directory or stdin/stdout bridge
IF Plandex auto-apply is enabled while imported text contains instruction-like payloads
mitigations: Keep the two agents in separate directories
Paste only minimal excerpts, not whole files
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: Plandex touches source code and can call external model providers, but spring-integration-samples exposes no sensitive data classes or shared workspace. With no documented shared filesystem or credentials overlap, leakage is limited and requires an explicit bridge.
conditions: IF source code from spring-integration-samples is copied into Plandex and sent to a model provider
IF both agents are run under the same filesystem workspace or credential store
mitigations: Avoid pasting secrets into either agent

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Plandex has filesystem write, shell, subprocess, and git-state modification; spring-integration-samples is a repository that may be edited or used as input. Even without explicit write capability on B, shared project state can still create conflicting changes if both touch the same checkout.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same git checkout
IF spring-integration-samples is edited while Plandex stages or applies changes
mitigations: Commit or stash before switching agents
requires-engineering: add locking around shared worktrees

D_cascading_error.rationale: Plandex can generate plans and apply changes, while spring-integration-samples provides example code that could be treated as authoritative input. If B's outputs are fed into A without verification, mistakes can cascade into incorrect edits or actions.
conditions: IF spring-integration-samples output is used as source material for Plandex plans
IF Plandex applies changes without human verification of the imported facts
mitigations: Require a human review step before apply
Limit A to read-only analysis first
requires-engineering: add validation gates before apply

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and touch source code only; no PHI, EU PII, residency, or retention mismatch is documented. The pairwise compliance pathway is therefore not evidenced beyond generic software handling.
conditions: IF either agent is repurposed to process regulated personal data
IF a deployment adds residency or retention constraints not present in these profiles
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the pair
Use separate environments for regulated workloads
